summary:
The Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao stands under the national framework of the Philippines. Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 13, the Bangsamoro Administrative Code, begun 29 March 2019, sets out the region's structures and rules of governance and guarantees religious freedom. Its justice-dispensation clause directs that justice be dispensed "in consonance with the Constitution, Shari'ah, traditional or tribal laws". Nothing in the regional code addresses gender identity or gender non-conformity.

A Shari'ah Justice Code proposed in the Bangsamoro Parliament on 14 July 2026 would widen Shari'ah jurisdiction beyond the personal-status field it has occupied since the Code of Muslim Personal Laws (Presidential Decree 1083, 1977), reaching into civil actions, Islamic commercial transactions, ta'tir offences and alternative dispute resolution. The proposal rests on the region's organic-law authority and on the 1977 Code of Personal and Family Relations. For a visitor, the practical consequence is that a dispute can be routed to a Shari'ah forum rather than a civil court, and the applicable law follows the forum.

Marriage, divorce, succession and family relations for Muslim residents remain governed by Shari'ah forums, with written opt-in clauses allowing civil entities to take on matters otherwise within that jurisdiction. A visitor married to a Muslim spouse therefore enters a legal-pluralist marriage regime in which the forum that hears a matter determines which body of personal law applies.
tangentialFactors: In August 2024 the national president signed a law creating three new Shari'ah judicial districts and 12 circuit courts, passed unanimously by the national legislature, which extends the Shari'ah court system beyond the Bangsamoro into majority-Christian northern Mindanao, Davao-region provinces, parts of the Visayas, Luzon and Metro Manila. The measure carries the region's Shari'ah personal-law regime onto a national footing. A publication reported local Christian-leader reaction to it in November 2024.
localsOnly: For Muslim residents of the region, marriage, divorce, succession and family relations are governed by Shari'ah forums under the 1977 Code of Personal and Family Relations; written opt-in clauses allow civil entities to take on matters otherwise within that jurisdiction. The proposed Shari'ah Justice Code runs to ten books and would extend Shari'ah jurisdiction into civil actions, Islamic commercial transactions, ta'tir offences and alternative dispute resolution.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources reviewed contain no regional instrument addressing gender identity, gender expression or SOGIE, and no regional anti-discrimination ordinance or documented regional enforcement incident. Whether the region has adopted any such measure is unresolved on the material reviewed.

How a Shari'ah forum would classify a marriage involving a trans spouse, or a relationship read as same-sex under birth-sex status, is not addressed in the sources.

The Shari'ah Justice Code was a proposal as of 14 July 2026; its enactment status is not recorded in the sources reviewed.
